## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (no finding or checklist FAIL at the critical threshold; one documentation criterion is not yet met)

The code and test changes are correct and ready to merge. The one open gap is that `docs/internal/mcp-server/transport.md` does not yet state the single-event-loop assumption that acceptance criterion 3 asks for, and the 4.1.5 rule grades that gap as a documentation-only Suggestion.
Rule applied: rule 6 — findings or checklist FAILs below the threshold remain → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (6)

<details><summary>6 items</summary>

1. `docs/internal/mcp-server/transport.md` line 115 (the "SQL execution" bullet) does not say that the slot limit, the wait limit and the saturation warning assume all SQL calls run on one event loop at a time. It also does not say that calls from a second loop running at the same time get their own slots and may wait in the shared executor's queue, where neither the wait limit nor the warning applies. Acceptance criterion 3 requires this statement in both the `sql_threads.py` module docstring and this page. The diff adds it only to the docstring (head `sql_threads.py` lines 22-27) and does not touch `transport.md`. The same bullet also does not mention the new warning logged for each rejected call, and the regression-coverage paragraph (line 125) does not list the new tests. (raised by 4/5 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: criterion 3 requires prose only; adding the sentence changes no output, branch or covered set of the SQL worker pool. git grep over the repository for 'transport.md' and 'docs/internal/mcp-server' finds only Markdown cross-links in other docs/internal pages and a docstring pointer at sql_threads.py:41, and no tool, lint, workflow or agent-instruction file reads the page. docs/internal is not published, and vendor-slice.sh:106 strips it. -->
2. The same `docs/internal/mcp-server/transport.md` line 115 gap, filed as comment drift: the page does not state the single-loop assumption or mention the per-rejection warning, while the module docstring now does. This finding is labelled differently, so it does not formally corroborate item 1. (raised by 1/5 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: same searches as item 1; no tool or agent reads transport.md for behavior, and docs/internal is not published. -->
3. `src/sqllens/agent/integrations/sql_threads.py` lines 115-121: the `ERROR` record written when a slot cannot be returned on a still-open loop ("A SQL worker slot could not be returned: %s") says the release failed but not what that means. The slot is never released, so the loop has one fewer slot for the rest of the process. After `SQL_WORKER_THREADS` such failures, every call waits 60 seconds and is rejected. Adding that consequence to the message would help an operator. (raised by 1/5 agents)
4. `tests/integration/test_slow_agent_run_responsiveness.py` line 139: the new test docstring "Issue #299 reported failures whenever several agent runs were active." records where the test came from rather than what a maintainer must not break. The module docstring (lines 14-16) already states what the test asserts. (raised by 1/5 agents)

Connect, ping, setup, execute, fetch and close all happen inside _run_sql_blocking (102-180) on a single worker. So SqlWorkersBusyError can only come from acquiring the slot for that single call, before any of it runs. No earlier call can execute the query before a rejected one, and the docstring 'the query never ran' holds. acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Each call that fails with `SqlWorkersBusyError` produces exactly one rejection `WARNING` record (distinct from the saturation warning) on the `sqllens.agent.integrations.sql_threads` logger, including rejections that occur within `SATURATION_WARNING_INTERVAL_S` of a saturation warning; a unit test that times out several queued calls in one burst sees one rejection record per rejected call. No rejection record contains the call's SQL, arguments or exception message.
- [ ] On Python 3.11 and 3.12, a unit test that grants a waiting call its slot and cancels that call in the same loop tick sees the caller raise `CancelledError`, the call never run, and the slot still available to a later call.
- [ ] The `sql_threads.py` module docstring and `docs/internal/mcp-server/transport.md` state that the slot limit, the wait limit and the saturation warning assume all SQL calls run on one event loop at a time, and that calls from a second concurrently running loop get their own slots and may wait in the shared executor's queue, where neither the wait limit nor the warning applies.
- [ ] When the release of a slot fails because its event loop is closed, no `ERROR` record is written on the `sqllens.agent.integrations.sql_threads` logger and nothing propagates; when scheduling the release raises a `RuntimeError` while the loop is still open, one `ERROR` record naming the exception type is written on that logger and nothing propagates. Unit tests cover both cases.
- [ ] A unit test makes `submit` raise and then shows that `SQL_WORKER_THREADS` calls on that loop all start without waiting for a slot.
- [ ] Every SQL worker pool test in `tests/unit/test_sql_runner_event_loop.py` runs on an executor no earlier test used.
- [ ] Every test under `tests/integration/` starts with `sqllens.tools._agent._AGENT_STATE` set to `None`, as every unit test already does.
- [ ] The `run_sql` docstrings of the SQLite, MySQL and Postgres runners list `SqlWorkersBusyError` under `Raises:`.
- [ ] An integration test holds two `query_database` runs, from two different conversations, open at the local model stand-in at the same time; while both are held, `/healthz` and `list_data_sources` on another session each answer within 2 s, and once released both runs return a result that is not an error.
- [ ] The change leaves the slot semaphore keyed per event loop and the worker executor process-wide, adds no file under `changelog.d/`, and leaves `changelog.d/300.fixed.md` unchanged, including its sentence that a query waiting more than a minute for a free worker fails with "All database workers are busy; try again shortly."
